title: Sprint weave catchup — kernel, KV cache & batching
content:
Sprint Weave Catchup — kernel, KV cache & batching
Sprint: 56 (Apr 12–16 2027)
Owners: Maya (kernel), Diego (kv-cache), Sana (batcher)

Quick summary:
- Focus this sprint: stabilize kernel scheduling change (soft-preempt), reduce KV shadow eviction spikes, and prototype adaptive micro-batching thresholding.
- Primary goal met: soft-preempt landed behind feature flag (PR #3421) and basic telemetry reporting is in.
- Main risk: rare p95 latency regressions under specific guest-model sequences when soft-preempt interleaves with KV-prefill.

Highlights / wins:
- Kernel: soft-preempt patch merged to canary, rollout started for 10% of requests. Initial telemetry shows 8% reduction in long-tail GPU stall periods.
- KV cache: implemented conservative backpressure counter to avoid mass-eviction cascades; early experiments reduced eviction churn by ~22% in lab traffic.
- Batching: adaptive-slice prototype detects high skew and reduces micro-batch timeouts from 12ms -> 6ms for hot routes; throughput preserved while lowering median latency.

Deep dives / notes from the whiteboard:
1) Kernel scheduling interactions (Maya)
   - Problem: previous strict-yield introduced starvation for long sequence decode tasks; soft-preempt yields earlier but keeps a token budget to finish a short tail.
   - Observed: when soft-preempt triggers during KV-prefill read, the kernel will requeue work onto a hot lane, sometimes causing the kernel handshake to retrigger a prefill.
   - Mitigation idea: add prefill-aware priority bit on handshake to defer prefill reentrant scheduling for 1ms window.
   - Action: Maya -> prototype guard (prefill-aware bit) in kernel shim. Target: POC by Apr 20.

2) KV cache eviction cascade (Diego)
   - Root cause hypothesis: sudden burst of large-head requests cause multiple prefills that advance LRU clock skew among partitions; eviction heuristics treat partitions independently leading to synchronized compaction waves.
   - Temporary fix deployed: global soft-throttle across partitions with jittered clock updates.
   - Next: explore partition-level watermarking and shadow-promote: when a prefill sees high contention, mark keys as "do-not-evict" for short TTL.
   - Action: Diego -> run A/B with shadow-promote on dev cluster; collect eviction_histogram and per-partition LRU-age. ETA: Apr 18.

3) Adaptive batching prototype (Sana)
   - Prototype detects heavy-skew routes by measuring arrival-variance over 500ms window; when skew > threshold, it switches to skew-aware sampler that favours latency-sensitive requests.
   - Observed tradeoff: favouring latency-sensitive requests increases cost slightly (less batch efficiency) but drops p95 by up to 15% for those routes. Need product signoff on cost/latency tradeoffs.
   - Action: Sana -> prepare short A/B deck for PMs (cost vs p95). ETA: Apr 16.

Metrics snapshot (canary, last 24h):
- p50 latency: 24ms (no change)
- p95 latency: 187ms (up 12ms on canary traffic) — correlated with specific multi-prefill sequences
- GPU stall %: down 8% on kernel-canary nodes
- KV eviction churn: down 22% in synthetic replay
- Batch sizes (hot routes): median 6 -> 5 after adaptive tuning

Incidents / anomalies observed:
- Apr 13 03:22 UTC: two short latency spikes (p95 doublings) on canary route /v1/chat/generate. Root cause: soft-preempt + reentrant prefill causing slight queue thrash.
  - Mitigated by rolling feature flag down to 5% while we patch guard.
  - Incident postmortem planned if recurrence >1 in 72h.

Decisions made:
- Keep soft-preempt behind feature flag; increase rollout to 25% only after prefill-aware guard implemented and validated. (Owner: Maya)
- Shadow-promote TTL default = 100ms for now; tune after A/B results. (Owner: Diego)
- Adaptive batching to be trialed on two routes (chat-short and chat-long) for 1 week. PMs to approve cost guard. (Owner: Sana)

Action items (owners and rough ETA):
- Maya: implement prefill-aware priority bit + unit tests. ETA: 2027-04-20.
- Diego: run A/B shadow-promote experiment, collect eviction_histogram. ETA: 2027-04-18.
- Sana: A/B deck for PMs (cost vs p95), include runbook option to revert. ETA: 2027-04-16.
- Evan: add more fine-grained tracing for kernel handshake event (trace id correlation). ETA: 2027-04-17.
- Rhea: update runbook for canary rollback thresholds (p95 > baseline + 10% OR error rate > 0.5%). ETA: 2027-04-15.

Blockers / open questions:
- Does prefill-aware priority introduce starvation for downstream long-lived batches? Need microbench for sustained long outputs. (Maya/Evan)
- Is the shadow-promote TTL of 100ms sufficient under high tail traffic? Risk: too long -> reduces cache agility. (Diego)
- PM signoff timeline on adaptive batching cost window. We need a hard upper bound on token-cost delta. (Sana/Product)

Parking lot (non-blocking ideas):
- Explore tiny per-request hints from client that mark sequences as latency-sensitive vs throughput-preferred. Could be opt-in per-route.
- Experiment with staggered LRU clocks (per-client group) to avoid synchronized evictions more generally.

Notes to self / meeting color:
- Keep notes in this doc; viral copy of metrics snapshot will go to #serving-runtime with a short TL;DR.
- We should add a short explainer PR linking kernel soft-preempt design doc to the canary telemetry dashboards for easier triage by SRE.

Next meeting: Apr 19 10:00 PT — focus: prefill-guard review + A/B eviction results

Appendix (quick links):

- JIRA: JIRA-RT-1287 (kernel soft-preempt)

-- End of catchup
